##### Power Normal Distribution {#sec-eda-power-normal-distribution}

**Probability Density Function**

The formula for the [probability density function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the standard form of the power normal distribution is

$$f(x; p) = p\,\phi(x)\,(\Phi(-x))^{p - 1} \qquad x, p > 0$$

where $p$ is the [shape parameter](#sec-eda-families-of-distributions) (also referred to as the power parameter), $\Phi$ is the cumulative distribution function of the [standard normal](#sec-eda-normal-distribution) distribution, and $\phi$ is the probability density function of the [standard normal](#sec-eda-normal-distribution) distribution.

As with other probability distributions, the power normal distribution can be transformed with a [location parameter](#sec-eda-location-and-scale-parameters), $\mu$, and a [scale parameter](#sec-eda-location-and-scale-parameters), $\sigma$. We omit the equation for the general form of the power normal distribution. Since the general form of probability functions can be [expressed in terms of the standard distribution](#sec-eda-location-and-scale-parameters), all subsequent formulas in this section are given for the standard form of the function.

The following is the plot of the power normal probability density function with four values of $p$: 0.5, 1, 2, and 5.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-power-normal-dist-pdf
#| fig-cap: "Power normal probability density function"
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

dpnorm <- function(x, p) p * dnorm(x) * (pnorm(-x))^(p - 1)

tibble(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401)) |>
  expand_grid(p = c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)) |>
  mutate(y = dpnorm(x, p),
         p = factor(p)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y, color = p)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "x", y = "f(x)", color = "p") +
  theme_light()
```

**Cumulative Distribution Function**

The formula for the [cumulative distribution function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the power normal distribution is

$$F(x; p) = 1 - (\Phi(-x))^{p} \qquad x, p > 0$$

where $\Phi$ is the cumulative distribution function of the standard [normal](#sec-eda-normal-distribution) distribution.

The following is the plot of the power normal cumulative distribution function with the same values of $p$ as the pdf plot above.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-power-normal-dist-cdf
#| fig-cap: "Power normal cumulative distribution function"
ppnorm <- function(x, p) 1 - (pnorm(-x))^p

tibble(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401)) |>
  expand_grid(p = c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)) |>
  mutate(y = ppnorm(x, p),
         p = factor(p)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y, color = p)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "x", y = "F(x)", color = "p") +
  theme_light()
```

**Percent Point Function**

The formula for the [percent point function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the power normal distribution is

$$G(f) = \Phi^{-1}\!\left(1 - (1 - f)^{1/p}\right) \qquad 0 < f < 1;\ p > 0$$

where $\Phi^{-1}$ is the percent point function of the standard [normal](#sec-eda-normal-distribution) distribution.

The following is the plot of the power normal percent point function with the same values of $p$ as the pdf plot above.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-power-normal-dist-ppf
#| fig-cap: "Power normal percent point function"
qpnorm <- function(f, p) qnorm(1 - (1 - f)^(1 / p))

tibble(p_prob = seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 401)) |>
  expand_grid(p = c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)) |>
  mutate(x = qpnorm(p_prob, p),
         p = factor(p)) |>
  ggplot(aes(p_prob, x, color = p)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = expression(alpha), y = expression(G(alpha)), color = "p") +
  theme_light()
```

**Hazard Function**

The formula for the [hazard function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the power normal distribution is

$$h(x; p) = \frac{p\,\phi(x)}{\Phi(-x)} \qquad x, p > 0$$

The following is the plot of the power normal hazard function with the same values of $p$ as the pdf plot above.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-power-normal-dist-hazard
#| fig-cap: "Power normal hazard function"
hpnorm <- function(x, p) p * dnorm(x) / pnorm(-x)

tibble(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401)) |>
  expand_grid(p = c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)) |>
  mutate(y = hpnorm(x, p),
         p = factor(p)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y, color = p)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "x", y = "h(x)", color = "p") +
  theme_light()
```

**Cumulative Hazard Function**

The formula for the [cumulative hazard function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the power normal distribution is

$$H(x; p) = -\log\!\left((\Phi(-x))^{p}\right) \qquad x, p > 0$$

The following is the plot of the power normal cumulative hazard function with the same values of $p$ as the pdf plot above.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-power-normal-dist-cumulative-hazard
#| fig-cap: "Power normal cumulative hazard function"
hpnorm_cum <- function(x, p) -log((pnorm(-x))^p)

tibble(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401)) |>
  expand_grid(p = c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)) |>
  mutate(y = hpnorm_cum(x, p),
         p = factor(p)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y, color = p)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "x", y = "H(x)", color = "p") +
  theme_light()
```

**Survival Function**

The formula for the [survival function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the power normal distribution is

$$S(x; p) = (\Phi(-x))^{p} \qquad x, p > 0$$

The following is the plot of the power normal survival function with the same values of $p$ as the pdf plot above.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-power-normal-dist-survival
#| fig-cap: "Power normal survival function"
spnorm <- function(x, p) (pnorm(-x))^p

tibble(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401)) |>
  expand_grid(p = c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)) |>
  mutate(y = spnorm(x, p),
         p = factor(p)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y, color = p)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "x", y = "S(x)", color = "p") +
  theme_light()
```

**Inverse Survival Function**

The formula for the [inverse survival function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the power normal distribution is

$$Z(f) = \Phi^{-1}\!\left(1 - f^{1/p}\right) \qquad 0 < f < 1;\ p > 0$$

The following is the plot of the power normal inverse survival function with the same values of $p$ as the pdf plot above.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-power-normal-dist-inverse-survival
#| fig-cap: "Power normal inverse survival function"
zpnorm <- function(f, p) qnorm(1 - f^(1 / p))

tibble(p_prob = seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 401)) |>
  expand_grid(p = c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)) |>
  mutate(z = zpnorm(p_prob, p),
         p = factor(p)) |>
  ggplot(aes(p_prob, z, color = p)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = expression(alpha), y = expression(Z(alpha)), color = "p") +
  theme_light()
```

**Common Statistics**

The statistics for the power normal distribution are complicated and require tables. Nelson [@Nelson2] discusses the mean, median, mode, and standard deviation of the power normal distribution and provides references to the appropriate tables.

**Software**

Most general purpose statistical software programs do not support the probability functions for the power normal distribution.
